_meta.role: Embedded Software Dev Engineer, Ring and Blink Devices

summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY. Built bare-metal embedded C firmware on ARM CPUs (Cortex-M4, STM32) with interrupt service routines, a low-level I2C driver and timer-triggered ADC, plus FreeRTOS task coordination over UART and PWM. Added Bluetooth wireless links, SPI/I2C/UART peripherals and hardware debugging and integration troubleshooting, and deploy TensorRT-optimized AI models on embedded Jetson devices.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.
Used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built a Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to STM32 over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: Robocon Competition Robot — Holonomic Drive & Encoder Odometry
bullets: Built closed-loop heading correction for a 4-wheel holonomic robot on Arduino Due: derived actual heading from dual-axis quadrature encoder odometry (2400 CPR, 2.9 cm wheels) and fed angular error back into rotation PWM, holding course during translation.
Implemented interrupt-driven quadrature decoding from first principles — a 4-bit A/B transition state machine on hardware interrupts — and drove four motor channels at 15 kHz PWM via DuePWM.
projects.note: SELECTION GUIDANCE, not resume text. Undergraduate robotics-club work at FCRIT, not professional experience. Include when the JD asks for motor control, encoders, odometry or closed-loop feedback — this is the only evidence for those. Otherwise prefer 'STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor' and the COFFIN capstone, which are stronger work. Never place it first, and never let it crowd out COFFIN on an edge-AI role.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Integrated faster-whisper STT (1.0–1.4s), Gemini intent classification (<500ms), TensorRT-optimized YOLO (5.2× speedup: 56.7→10.9 ms, 17.6→92 FPS vs eager PyTorch) for visual servoing, and dual VL53L0X ToF sensors (camera range-gate + gripper-ToF-triggered close at 25 mm) for contact-aware grasping via TCA9548A I2C mux.
Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end voice-to-picked latency.
